_comment: forest: Map 3. Authored in WORLD coordinates, instance at identity: grass lane r 46.7..57.3 at y 23.0 (as map 1), the pit bank down to a dark floor at y -11.05 (r 42) buried under the fog, a leaf wall from r 57.3 up to the lane roof at y 38.0 (forest_seam.CEIL_Z, 15 m over the grass), the leaf roof itself r 60 in to the pit lip at 46.7 sagging 0.5 m mid-span and lumped +-0.55 faces DOWN, and on that roof's inner rim the CELL DRUM: r 46.70..47.60, y 38.0 up to the seam at 50.0, three tiers of 17 barred mouths (sills 38.5 / 42.7 / 46.9) facing the tower. Ryan: 'make the roof higher, so make it like a dome that collapses in the middle where the tree is, and so theres still like a ring of cells above where the player runs.' So the drum's HEAD ring IS forest_seam.seam_ring() -- 240 points, column i = point i, the same floats forest_tree.glb's crown sheet ends on -- and from there the tower's own crown sweeps INWARD AND DOWN to its rim at r 11, y 34.1: the dome is high at the ring and collapsed where the tree holds it. The 240 edges at r 47.6 are open in THIS mesh because the other model carries the roof on from there. Five sun wells in the lane roof (three shafts land on the lane, two fall into the ravine), nothing hung under them any more (Ryan: 'get rid of the like, hanging trees where the streaks of light come from'), 12 forest trunks standing in the wall, THREE tiers of lane-facing cells cut into the wall (12 / 22 / 23 mouths, sills y 23.3 / 28.6 / 33.0) and 36 into the pit bank, a thicket of thorny brambles out of the pit floor, ferns and hummocks along the wall foot and the lip only. THIRTEEN surfaces on ForestGround, one tiling sheet per class through lib/texel.py (grass, verge, path, edge, leaf, shade, sun, fern, bark, earth, cell, root, lamp), world-projected at 0.05 m per texel, no atlas windows. `lamp` is the new one and the only emissive sheet in the map: every one of the 144 cells' BACK FACE wears it, so each cell carries its own small dim light (Ryan) at no light, no draw call and no triangle -- the back face was always there. ForestRaysSolid and ForestRaysSoft are the sun-ray shafts (one per sun well, three crossed vanes, same geometry, tint and feather in COLOR_0, pale / faint) behind MESH_RAYS, one surface each. ForestFog is the pit's fog and now the pit's floor is buried in it: 14 stacked translucent layers with tint and alpha in COLOR_0, alpha rising with depth to a solid slab low down, the material's disable_fog keeping the Environment's pale depth fog from repainting it, so a vertical ray reaches the floor at 0.138 % transmittance and the ravine reads bottomless. One surface (GL Compatibility has no fog volumes). ForestCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (flat lane, pit cone, pit floor, flat wall r 57.3 to y 38.0, the flat ceiling annulus r 57.3..46.7 at y 38.0; the drum and the dome above it are out of reach and carry none); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
